import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

# Extract the most recent data (2015) for analysis
education_expenditure = adjusted_savings_df[['Country Group', 'Country Code', '2015 [YR2015]']]
gni_per_capita = gni_per_capita_df[['Country Group', 'Country Code', '2015 [YR2015]']]
exports = exports_df[['Country Group', 'Country Code', '2015 [YR2015]']]

# Merge the datasets on 'Country Group' and 'Country Code'
merged_data = pd.merge(education_expenditure, gni_per_capita, on=['Country Group', 'Country Code'], how='inner')
merged_data = pd.merge(merged_data, exports, on=['Country Group', 'Country Code'], how='inner')

# Rename columns for clarity
merged_data.columns = ['Country Group', 'Country Code', 'Education_Expenditure', 'GNI_per_Capita', 'Exports_Growth']

# Display the merged data
merged_data.head()

# Perform correlation analysis
correlation_matrix = merged_data[['Education_Expenditure', 'GNI_per_Capita', 'Exports_Growth']].corr()
correlation_matrix

# Perform linear regression to analyze the relationship between education expenditure and GNI per capita
X = merged_data[['Education_Expenditure']]
y = merged_data['GNI_per_Capita']

model.fit(X, y)
coefficient = model.coef_[0]
intercept = model.intercept_

y = merged_data['Exports_Growth']
